# UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales
Source: https://llmsx.org/tree/ux-measurement-usability-metrics-and-psychometric-scales/

# UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-09 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] SUS is an overall post-test perceived-usability questionnaire; SEQ is a post-task rating of the difficulty of the task just attempted. Choose the instrument according to the level of experience being evaluated. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/ · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://measuringu.com/papers/Sauro_Dumas_CHI2009.pdf

## Structure and components

- [statement] SUS contains 10 items with five response options. Its transformed score ranges from 0 to 100 and is not a percentage or a percentile rank. (medium confidence) — https://measuringu.com/sus/ · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/

## How it works

- [statement] SEQ asks about perceived task difficulty immediately after each task, whereas SUS concerns the overall session; use the task-level question to compare tasks, keeping tasks comparable when benchmarking. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/ · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://measuringu.com/papers/Sauro_Dumas_CHI2009.pdf
- [statement] UMUX-LITE uses two positively worded items about capabilities meeting requirements and ease of use. Its original researchers reported concurrent validity with SUS in two surveys and proposed it as a shorter alternative when a longer questionnaire is undesirable. (medium confidence) — https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2470654.2481287 · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://measuringu.com/umux-lite/
- [statement] Treat validation as evidence for a particular instrument and context. The Greek UMUX-LITE study found good reliability and concurrent validity on the websites it studied, while explicitly limiting generalization because it tested only two systems of the same type. (low confidence) — https://dl.acm.org/doi/fullHtml/10.1145/3635059.3635075
- [statement] UMUX-Lite asks whether the system’s capabilities meet the respondent’s requirements and whether the system is easy to use. Its two positive items cover perceived usefulness and ease of use; it is a shorter alternative when questionnaire burden matters. (low confidence) — https://measuringu.com/umux-lite/
- [statement] Satisfaction scores do not explain the cause of a usability problem. Combine questionnaire scores with observed performance and follow-up investigation before deciding what design change to make. (medium confidence) — https://measuringu.com/sus/ · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Do not use a satisfaction score alone to diagnose an interface failure or assume that a favorable SUS score proves successful task performance. Combine ratings with observed performance and investigation of the problems. (medium confidence) — https://measuringu.com/sus/ · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/
- [statement] Use Goals–Signals–Metrics to make measurement actionable: articulate the product or feature goal, identify behavior or attitudes that signal success or failure, then define specific metrics. The official publication describes the framework as a way to connect product goals and metrics. (medium confidence) — https://research.google.com/pubs/archive/36299.pdf · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://research.google/pubs/measuring-the-user-experience-on-a-large-scale-user-centered-metrics-for-web-applications/
- [statement] Small samples limit inference even when an instrument is reliable. Sauro recommends a confidence interval around the sample SUS score because small samples produce imprecise population estimates; Sauro and Dumas found low detection rates for post-task instruments at small sample sizes in their experiment. (medium confidence) — https://measuringu.com/sus/ · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://measuringu.com/papers/Sauro_Dumas_CHI2009.pdf
- [statement] The Goals–Signals–Metrics process starts with a product or feature goal, identifies behavioral or attitudinal signals of success or failure, and translates them into metrics. Prefer signals specific to the goal, normalize raw counts when user-base growth would distort interpretation, and check logging coverage and automated traffic. (low confidence) — https://research.google.com/pubs/archive/36299.pdf

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Measure task effectiveness with completion and errors, efficiency with completion time, and perceived usability with questionnaires; subjective ratings complement observed performance rather than replacing it. (medium confidence) — https://research.google.com/pubs/archive/36299.pdf · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/
- [statement] SUS is a ten-item, five-response-option questionnaire for perceived usability; administer it after the session to assess overall impressions rather than the difficulty of an individual task. (medium confidence) — https://measuringu.com/sus/ · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/
- [statement] A SUS score on its zero-to-one-hundred scale is not a percentage or a percentile. Interpret it against a relevant score distribution; norms describe relative standing rather than a universal usability pass mark. (medium confidence) — https://measuringu.com/sus/ · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/
- [statement] Keep reliability, validity, and precision separate: consistency of questionnaire responses differs from measuring the intended construct, and a small sample can still give an imprecise population estimate. MeasuringU recommends a confidence interval around the sample SUS score. (low confidence) — https://measuringu.com/sus/
- [statement] Google’s HEART framework groups metrics into Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention, and Task success. These are selectable categories rather than a requirement to track every category for every product. (low confidence) — https://research.google.com/pubs/archive/36299.pdf
- [statement] MeasuringU says small SUS samples can retain reliable responses but yield imprecise population estimates and recommends confidence intervals. NN/g gives stricter practitioner advice against using numerical results from very small qualitative samples for design decisions. These positions warrant separating measurement reliability from inference precision rather than adopting a universal sample-size cutoff. (low confidence) — https://measuringu.com/sus/ · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/
- [statement] The often-cited average SUS score of 68 comes from Sauro’s historical set of 500 studies. Interpret it as a reference distribution, with percentile conversion as a separate operation, rather than treating the raw score as a percentage. (low confidence) — https://measuringu.com/sus/
- [statement] UMUX-Lite can be reported as separate item means, an aggregate, or a regression-based SUS-equivalent estimate. Label that conversion explicitly: the cited methodological account describes continued evaluation and refinement rather than establishing unconditional interchangeability with SUS. (low confidence) — https://measuringu.com/umux-lite/
- [statement] Analytics proxies need interpretation: Google’s paper notes that increased page views can indicate either popularity or confusion. Its authors recommend triangulating metrics with other research rather than allowing dashboard measures to stand alone. (low confidence) — https://research.google.com/pubs/archive/36299.pdf

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Report which UMUX-LITE scoring convention and response scale you used. The original study adjusted the two-item score with regression to align with SUS; the practitioner guide also describes unadjusted item means and SUS-equivalent scores, so these outputs should not be silently interchanged. (medium confidence) — https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2470654.2481287 · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://measuringu.com/umux-lite/
- [statement] Choose metrics whose interpretation follows the user goal. The HEART paper warns that more page views can reflect popularity or confusion, recommends normalizing counts as the user base grows, and calls for filtering automated traffic and checking instrumentation coverage. (low confidence) — https://research.google.com/pubs/archive/36299.pdf
- [statement] The SEQ uses a seven-point easy–difficult rating immediately after a task. Comparisons across systems require comparable tasks; within a system it can identify relatively difficult task flows. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/
- [statement] In their 2009 experiment, Sauro and Dumas found that the seven-point Likert task-difficulty question was easy to administer, correlated with other measures, and was as sensitive as their online mental-effort question. These findings concern the tasks and products studied. (low confidence) — https://measuringu.com/papers/Sauro_Dumas_CHI2009.pdf
- [statement] Validity concerns whether an instrument measures its intended construct; reliability concerns response consistency; sensitivity concerns detecting meaningful differences. These are distinct from the precision of a population estimate. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/measuring-perceived-usability/ · keywords: UX measurement, usability metrics and psychometric scales · also: https://measuringu.com/sus/
